- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and model shows rising trend, cap upward momentum; if sentiment turns neutral, avoid sharp reversals.
- Model often overcorrects after sharp price spikes — apply a 3–5 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.
- In periods of high volatility or sentiment divergence, reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to hold or overestimate — adjust downward by 2–4% per day.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, reduce forecast confidence and apply smoothing filter.
